topic: Can the filter's suppression of 19th harmonics improve transponder power efficiency in dense payload configurations?
consensus_response: The filter's suppression of 19th harmonics can improve transponder power efficiency in dense payload configurations by reducing non-linear distortions in high-power amplifiers. The physical mechanism involves the array factor and beam pattern of the amplifier. When harmonics are suppressed, the power density in the amplifier is more evenly distributed, reducing the risk of saturation and non-linear distortions. This spacing, typically by 0.5λ, ensures that the power is spread out, minimizing the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) and improving the amplifier's linearity. Consequently, the amplifier operates closer to its linear region, reducing intermodulation products and enhancing overall power efficiency. The interleaving effect in dense payload configurations modifies the amplifier's array factor and beam pattern by distributing symbols across multiple carriers. This distribution reduces the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), decreasing the drive level of the high power amplifier (HPA). Lower drive levels result in reduced non-linear distortions, as the HPA operates closer to its linear region. This modification reduces intermodulation products (IMD), adjacent channel interference (ACI), and inter symbol interference (ISI), improving transponder power efficiency.
